raw_draft.tldr: Corn's US sheet is the tight one and wheat's is the loose one: corn's stocks-to-use sits at 12.14% of domestic use [N11], in the 16th percentile of its own record [N49] and past the desk's tight line, against 65.22% for all-classes US wheat [N12] — so the feed-substitution edge runs in wheat's favour, with corn the dearer grain per bushel ([N63] 527.5 US cents/bushel for December 2026 corn against [N69] 707 for December 2026 CBOT srw wheat, a gap the record prints only as the spread [N13] of -179.5 US cents/bushel, corn under wheat). Corn's own reading count leans four up, three down beside a front price in the 94th percentile of its sessions [N68] and up 88 US cents over sixty-three sessions [N67]; wheat's leans two up, seven down beside [N73] and a collapsed harvested area [N14], so on the pair I lean corn-supportive and wheat's flat price carried by acreage, not by feed demand.
raw_draft.mechanism:
## Mechanism
The tracked link is two-way and opposite in sign. Cheap feed wheat substitutes for corn in rations, pulling corn feed demand down; higher corn prices lift the feed-wheat floor and support wheat. Which leg dominates is set by the relative price, and on this settle corn sits under wheat [N13] — meaning wheat is not the cheap ration grain here, so the substitution channel is not currently draining corn feed demand.

Corn's supportive readings: export shipments at 1,900 1000 MT in the week to 17 September 2026 [N38], ahead of its band, running into a stocks-to-use ratio past the tight line [N47] — the model records these two as amplifying each other, fast exports against a thin buffer. That is two of the three conditions the demand-pull pattern names. Against it, the warm-phase Pacific reading at +1.8 degC [N17], +2.4 sigma [N18], is declared to push corn the other way on a one-to-three-quarter lag.

Wheat's own sheet is loose on stocks but its area reading is the largest move on this board: 12.97 M ha [N14], 1st percentile [N16], falling two years. Low area is price-supportive with a one-to-three-quarter lag; weak shipments at 43.1 1000 MT [N54], behind, offset it.

## Cross-commodity
- CBOT corn, United States: 12.14% of domestic use [N11].
- Wheat, all classes, United States: 65.22% of domestic use [N12].
Each on its own marketing year; corn's buffer is razor-thin against wheat's ample cushion, so a corn supply shock is convex and right-tailed while wheat's absorbs one. The largest moves here are also declared on CME palm oil, in that market's own direction and lag.

## The record
Corn: production 15,800 Million Bushels [N1], ending stocks 1,567 [N2], domestic use 12,905 [N3], farm price 4.8 $/bu [N4] (2026/27 USDA projection). Wheat: production 1,531 [N5], ending stocks 717 [N6], domestic use 1,099 [N7], farm price 6.4 $/bu [N8]. Feed use runs 151,137 1000 MT corn [N9] against 2,177 for wheat [N10]. Past episode: the season-average corn farm price, a survey-based USDA actual, rose from $3.56/bu [N90] to $4.53/bu [N91]. The corn chain the record follows — fertilizer into area into stocks into price — is dark at two links; its fertilizer reading [N50] runs against the direction the model expects. Dated documents reach only 2024-04-24; the feed-substitution items are older ([E1] 2021, [E4] 2011), so the mechanism is documented but not current.

## What to watch
- Warm-phase Pacific anomaly [N17]: +1.8 degC, July 2026, past the strong line, eight months rising; effect window 2026-10-31 to 2027-04-30; wrong if the next print turns back inside 1.5 degC.
- US wheat harvested area [N14]: 12.97 M ha, known 2026-09-11, bottom decile; wrong if the next print returns it to mid-record.
- Blended fertilizer reading [N51]: -0.5 sigma, August 2026, four months falling toward the depressed line; window 2026-11-01 to 2027-05-01; wrong if the run breaks first.
Left aside: the palm oil spillover, which belongs to that market.
